verdict.rationale: Ubuntu Desktop is an operating system you download and install on your own hardware. First-party docs cover installing it in place of or alongside Windows, creating a bootable USB, and running it on older machines and Raspberry Pi, so the user runs the core product entirely on their own machines. Missing for 10: evidence of source availability or open licensing (the openness angle), evidence on self-hosting the package archive or update mirrors, and independent or hands-on corroboration of installation.
